test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user can navigate to the Holidays page
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with a valid account.
2. Navigate to Calendar > Holidays from the main menu.
test_cases.expected: The Holidays page loads. The page title reads 'Holidays' with the eyebrow 'Holidays'. The subtitle 'Manage public and bank holidays across locations for your organisation.' is visible.

test_cases.scenario: Page header, filters, and table are rendered on load
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
test_cases.expected: The page shows a search field, Location filter, Year filter, and an 'Add Holiday' button. The holidays table is rendered with columns: Name, Date, Location, Code, Created.

test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected away from the Holidays page
test_cases.steps: 1. Log out or open the Holidays page URL in an incognito window without logging in.
test_cases.expected: The user is redirected to the login page and cannot view any holiday data.

test_cases.scenario: User with manage permissions sees the Add Holiday button
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with permission to manage holidays.
2. Navigate to Calendar > Holidays.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Holiday' button is visible in the page header actions area.

test_cases.scenario: Read-only user does not see Add, Edit, or Delete controls
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with read-only access.
2. Navigate to Calendar > Holidays.
test_cases.expected: The 'Add Holiday' button is not visible. No Edit or Delete action buttons appear in the table rows.

test_cases.scenario: Breadcrumb reflects Calendar > Holidays hierarchy
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Calendar > Holidays.
test_cases.expected: The breadcrumb trail shows the correct hierarchy leading to the Holidays page.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays list loads and displays existing records
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Calendar > Holidays.
test_cases.expected: All existing holidays are displayed in the table. Each row shows: Name, Date, Location, Code, and Created date.

test_cases.scenario: Table displays correct columns in correct order
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Observe the table column headers.
test_cases.expected: Columns appear in order: Name, Date, Location, Code, Created. Name and Date are sortable. Location, Code, and Created are present (some hidden on mobile).

test_cases.scenario: Search by holiday name filters the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Type part of a holiday name into the search field.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only holidays whose names match the search term. Non-matching holidays are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Search with no matching results shows empty state
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Type a name that does not match any holiday into the search field.
test_cases.expected: The table shows an empty state message indicating no results were found.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the search field restores the full holiday list
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Type a search term that filters results.
3. Clear the search field.
test_cases.expected: The full list of holidays is restored without any name filter applied.

test_cases.scenario: Filter by Location shows only holidays for that location
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Location filter and select a specific location.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only holidays associated with the selected location. Holidays for other locations are not shown.

test_cases.scenario: Filter by Year shows only holidays in that year
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Year filter and select a specific year.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to show only holidays whose dates fall within the selected year.

test_cases.scenario: Combining Search, Location, and Year filters narrows results correctly
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Select a location from the Location filter.
3. Select a year from the Year filter.
4. Type a partial name into the search field.
test_cases.expected: The table shows only holidays matching all three criteria simultaneously — name, location, and year all applied together.

test_cases.scenario: Sort by Name (ascending and descending)
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Name column header once.
3. Click the Name column header again.
test_cases.expected: First click sorts the holiday list alphabetically by name (A–Z). Second click sorts in reverse order (Z–A).

test_cases.scenario: Sort by Date (ascending and descending)
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Date column header once.
3. Click the Date column header again.
test_cases.expected: First click sorts holidays by date from earliest to latest. Second click sorts from latest to earliest.

test_cases.scenario: Sort by Created date (ascending and descending)
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Created column header once.
3. Click the Created column header again.
test_cases.expected: Holidays are sorted by creation date in ascending then descending order.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination controls work correctly when more than one page of holidays exists
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page when more holidays exist than the default page size.
2. Click the next page button.
3. Click the previous page button.
test_cases.expected: Navigation between pages works correctly. Each page shows the correct subset of holidays. Page indicator updates accordingly.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a table row opens the view drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click anywhere on a holiday row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: The view drawer slides open on the right showing the full details of the selected holiday.

test_cases.scenario: Edit action button is visible and accessible for each row
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Hover over or expand the actions for a holiday row.
test_cases.expected: An Edit action button is visible for each holiday row.

test_cases.scenario: Delete action button is visible and accessible for each row
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Hover over or expand the actions for a holiday row.
test_cases.expected: A Delete action button is visible for each holiday row.

test_cases.scenario: No Toggle (activate/deactivate) action appears for holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Inspect the available row actions for any holiday.
test_cases.expected: No Toggle, Activate, or Deactivate action is present. Holidays have no active/inactive status.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Add Holiday opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the 'Add Holiday' button.
test_cases.expected: The create drawer slides open from the right side of the screen. The form is empty and ready for input.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer contains all required form fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the 'Add Holiday' button to open the create drawer.
2. Observe the form fields.
test_cases.expected: The drawer contains: Name field (with character counter), Date picker, and Location dropdown. All three fields are required.

test_cases.scenario: Create a holiday with all required fields filled
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Add Holiday'.
2. Enter a holiday name (e.g. 'Christmas Day').
3. Select a date.
4. Select a location.
5. Click the primary submit button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast notification appears. The new holiday appears in the table list.

test_cases.scenario: Newly created holiday appears in the list immediately
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a new holiday with a unique name.
2. Observe the holidays table after creation.
test_cases.expected: The new holiday row is visible in the table without needing to refresh the page.

test_cases.scenario: Name field is required — form shows validation error when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Leave the Name field empty.
3. Fill in Date and Location.
4. Click the submit button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Name field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Date field is required — form shows validation error when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in Name and Location.
3. Leave the Date field empty.
4. Click the submit button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Date field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Location field is required — form shows validation error when empty
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in Name and Date.
3. Leave the Location field empty.
4. Click the submit button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Location field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Name field enforces 120-character maximum
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Type more than 120 characters into the Name field.
test_cases.expected: Input is limited to 120 characters. The character counter reflects the remaining characters and does not allow exceeding the limit.

test_cases.scenario: Name field character counter updates as user types
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Type characters into the Name field one at a time.
test_cases.expected: A character counter is visible below or near the Name field. It updates in real time showing how many characters have been used or remain of the 120-character limit.

test_cases.scenario: Creating a holiday with a name that already exists for the same date and location
test_cases.steps:
1. Note an existing holiday's name, date, and location.
2. Open the create drawer.
3. Enter the exact same name, date, and location.
4. Click submit.
test_cases.expected: The form shows an error or the system prevents creating a duplicate holiday for the same name, date, and location combination.

test_cases.scenario: Closing the create drawer discards entered data
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in Name, Date, and Location.
3. Close the drawer by clicking the X or close button without submitting.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No holiday is created. If opened again, the form is empty.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer closes automatically after successful submission
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in all required fields with valid values.
3. Click the submit button.
test_cases.expected: After a successful save, the drawer closes automatically without requiring the user to close it manually.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast notification appears after creating a holiday
test_cases.steps: 1. Create a holiday with valid data and submit.
test_cases.expected: A success toast notification appears briefly confirming the holiday was created.

test_cases.scenario: Same holiday name can be created for different locations
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a holiday named 'New Year' for Location A.
2. Create another holiday named 'New Year' for Location B.
test_cases.expected: Both holidays are created successfully. The same holiday name can exist across different locations.

test_cases.scenario: Submit button shows busy/loading state during creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Fill in all required fields.
3. Click the submit button and observe it immediately.
test_cases.expected: The submit button shows a loading/busy indicator while the request is in progress. It is not clickable again until the operation completes.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a holiday row opens the view drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click on any holiday row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: The view drawer opens on the right side displaying the selected holiday's details.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer displays all expected detail fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Click on a holiday row to open the view drawer.
2. Observe all fields shown in the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer displays: Name, Date, Location, Code (displayed as code/monospace), Created (meta), Created by (meta).

test_cases.scenario: Code field is displayed in monospace/code style in the view drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the view drawer for any holiday.
2. Locate the Code field.
test_cases.expected: The Code field is rendered in a monospace or code-styled format, visually distinct from regular text fields.

test_cases.scenario: Created and Created by metadata fields are accurate
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a new holiday.
2. Click the row to open its view drawer.
3. Inspect the Created and Created by fields.
test_cases.expected: Created shows the date and time when the holiday was created. Created by shows the name of the user who created it.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer footer shows Edit holiday button for permissioned users
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with manage permissions.
2. Open the view drawer for any holiday.
test_cases.expected: The footer of the view drawer contains an 'Edit holiday' button for users who have permission to edit.

test_cases.scenario: Edit holiday button in view drawer opens the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the view drawer for a holiday.
2. Click the 'Edit holiday' button in the footer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer closes and the edit drawer opens, pre-populated with the same holiday's current data.

test_cases.scenario: Close button in view drawer footer closes the drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the view drawer for a holiday.
2. Click the 'Close' button in the footer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer closes and the user is returned to the holidays list without any changes.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer does not show Edit button for read-only users
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a read-only user.
2. Click on any holiday row to open the view drawer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer opens showing holiday details but the 'Edit holiday' button is not present in the footer.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Edit action button opens the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Edit action button on a holiday row.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer opens and is pre-populated with the selected holiday's current name, date, and location.

test_cases.scenario: Edit drawer pre-populates all fields with current holiday data
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday with known values.
2. Observe the Name, Date, and Location fields.
test_cases.expected: The Name field shows the current holiday name. The Date field shows the current date. The Location field shows the currently assigned location.

test_cases.scenario: Edit the holiday name and save successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Clear the Name field and enter a new valid name.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The updated holiday name is reflected in the table list. A success toast notification appears.

test_cases.scenario: Edit the holiday date and save successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Change the Date to a different valid date.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The updated date is reflected in the table list. A success toast notification appears.

test_cases.scenario: Edit the holiday location and save successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Change the Location to a different location.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The updated location is reflected in the table list. A success toast notification appears.

test_cases.scenario: Saved changes are reflected immediately in the holidays list
test_cases.steps:
1. Edit a holiday's name to a new value.
2. Save and observe the table.
test_cases.expected: The row in the table updates immediately to show the new name without requiring a page refresh.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast appears after saving holiday edits
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Make a change to any field.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: A success toast notification appears confirming the holiday was updated.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the Name field and saving shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Clear the Name field entirely.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Name field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the Date field and saving shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Clear the Date field.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Date field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Clearing the Location field and saving shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Clear or deselect the Location.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The form does not submit. A validation error is shown under the Location field indicating it is required.

test_cases.scenario: Closing the edit drawer without saving discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a holiday.
2. Change the name to something different.
3. Close the drawer without clicking save.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The holiday's original name is unchanged in the table list.

test_cases.scenario: Save button shows busy/loading state during the update
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer and make a change.
2. Click the save button and observe immediately.
test_cases.expected: The save button shows a loading/busy indicator while the request is processing and cannot be clicked again until the operation completes.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Delete action button shows a confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Click the Delete action button on any holiday row.
test_cases.expected: A confirmation modal appears asking the user to confirm the deletion. It mentions the holiday name.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal displays the holiday name
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Delete action button on a holiday named 'Christmas Day'.
2. Observe the confirmation modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal text includes the holiday name ('Christmas Day') so the user can confirm they are deleting the correct record.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the holiday from the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a holiday.
2. Click the confirm/delete button in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The holiday is removed from the table. A success toast notification confirms the deletion.

test_cases.scenario: Success toast appears after confirming deletion
test_cases.steps: 1. Delete a holiday and confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: A success toast notification appears briefly confirming that the holiday has been deleted.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the delete modal keeps the holiday intact
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a holiday.
2. Click the Cancel button in the confirmation modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The holiday remains in the table list and no changes are made.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal closes after cancellation
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a holiday.
2. Click Cancel in the confirmation modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes cleanly. The user is returned to the holidays list with the holiday still present.

test_cases.scenario: No Activate or Deactivate option exists for holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Review all available actions for any holiday row.
test_cases.expected: Only Edit and Delete actions are available. There are no Activate or Deactivate options since holidays do not have an active/inactive status.

test_cases.scenario: Import button is visible on the Holidays page
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Holidays page with manage permissions.
test_cases.expected: An Import button is visible in the page header actions area alongside the Add Holiday button.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Import button opens the import view
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Import button on the Holidays page.
test_cases.expected: The import view opens, providing options to download a sample file, upload a file, and review import specs.

test_cases.scenario: Sample import file can be downloaded
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Click the download sample file link or button.
test_cases.expected: A sample CSV or compatible file is downloaded that demonstrates the expected import format for holidays.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading a valid import file succeeds and adds holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Upload a correctly formatted file containing valid holiday data.
3. Confirm the import.
test_cases.expected: The import completes successfully. The imported holidays appear in the holidays list. A success message shows the number of records imported.

test_cases.scenario: Import success message shows the count of imported holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a file containing multiple holiday records.
2. Observe the result message after import completes.
test_cases.expected: The import result shows how many holidays were successfully imported.

test_cases.scenario: Uploading an invalid file format shows an error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Upload a file with an unsupported format (e.g., a PDF or image file).
test_cases.expected: An error message is shown indicating the file format is not supported. No holidays are imported.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays list refreshes after a successful import
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a valid file with new holidays.
2. Observe the holidays table after import completes.
test_cases.expected: The holidays table automatically refreshes and shows the newly imported holidays without requiring a manual page reload.

test_cases.scenario: Import view can be closed without importing
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the import view.
2. Close it without uploading a file.
test_cases.expected: The import view closes cleanly. No data is changed and the holidays list remains unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Export button is visible on the Holidays page
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Holidays page with manage permissions.
test_cases.expected: An Export button is visible in the page header actions area.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Export button opens the export view
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Export button on the Holidays page.
test_cases.expected: The export view opens, allowing the user to configure and trigger the export.

test_cases.scenario: Triggering the export downloads a file
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Confirm or click the export/download button.
test_cases.expected: A file is downloaded to the user's device containing the holiday data.

test_cases.scenario: Exported file contains the correct holiday data
test_cases.steps:
1. Export the holidays.
2. Open the downloaded file.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains all holidays currently visible in the list, with columns for Name, Date, Location, and Code at minimum.

test_cases.scenario: Export view can be closed without exporting
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the export view.
2. Close it without initiating an export.
test_cases.expected: The export view closes cleanly without downloading any file.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays page is navigable using keyboard only
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Use only the Tab and Enter keys to navigate the page, open the create drawer, and fill in form fields.
test_cases.expected: All interactive elements — filters, table rows, buttons, and form fields — are reachable and operable via keyboard navigation.

test_cases.scenario: Create and edit drawers are keyboard accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer using keyboard navigation.
2. Tab through all form fields and submit using the keyboard.
test_cases.expected: Focus moves logically through the Name, Date, and Location fields. The submit button is reachable and activatable via keyboard.

test_cases.scenario: Modals (delete confirmation) are keyboard accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Trigger the delete confirmation modal via keyboard.
2. Use Tab to navigate between Cancel and Confirm buttons.
3. Press Enter to confirm.
test_cases.expected: Focus is trapped within the modal while it is open. Both Cancel and Confirm buttons are reachable via Tab. Pressing Enter on the focused button activates it.

test_cases.scenario: Validation error messages are descriptive and clear
test_cases.steps:
1. Attempt to submit the create form with all fields empty.
2. Read the validation error messages that appear.
test_cases.expected: Validation messages are clear, human-readable, and tell the user exactly what is missing or incorrect (e.g. 'Name is required').

test_cases.scenario: No sensitive internal information is exposed in the UI or error messages
test_cases.steps:
1. Trigger various error states on the Holidays page (invalid input, server errors).
2. Observe all error messages shown to the user.
test_cases.expected: Error messages are user-friendly and do not expose stack traces, internal IDs, database queries, or server configuration details.

test_cases.scenario: Session is required to access and modify holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Log out.
2. Attempt to access the Holidays page directly via URL.
test_cases.expected: The user is redirected to the login page. Holiday data is not accessible without an active session.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays page loads within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Holidays page on a normal connection.
test_cases.expected: The page and its holiday data load within a reasonable time (typically under 3 seconds on a standard connection).

test_cases.scenario: Drawers close cleanly and release focus back to the page
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Close the drawer without submitting.
3. Observe focus behaviour.
test_cases.expected: When the drawer closes, focus is returned to a logical element on the main page (such as the Add Holiday button).

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible on desktop screen widths
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Holidays page on a desktop browser (viewport ≥ 1280px).
2. Observe the table columns.
test_cases.expected: All columns are visible: Name, Date, Location, Code, and Created.

test_cases.scenario: Filters are displayed inline above the table on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. View the Holidays page on a desktop viewport.
test_cases.expected: The Search field, Location filter, and Year filter are displayed in a horizontal filter bar above the holidays table.

test_cases.scenario: Drawers open in a side panel overlay on desktop
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Add Holiday' on a desktop browser.
2. Observe how the drawer appears.
test_cases.expected: The create drawer slides in from the right as a side panel. The main page content is still partially visible behind it.

test_cases.scenario: Row action buttons are visible in the table on desktop
test_cases.steps:
1. View the holidays table on desktop.
2. Observe the last column of each row.
test_cases.expected: Edit and Delete action buttons are displayed directly in the row actions column, accessible without additional clicks.

test_cases.scenario: Page layout does not overflow or break at 1280px width
test_cases.steps:
1. Set browser width to 1280px.
2. Navigate to the Holidays page and interact with create/edit drawers.
test_cases.expected: All page elements, the table, filters, and drawers display without horizontal overflow, clipping, or layout breakage.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays page loads and is usable on a mobile device
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Holidays page on a mobile device or emulator (viewport ≤ 768px).
test_cases.expected: The page loads correctly and is navigable. The table, filters, and header buttons are visible and usable.

test_cases.scenario: Location, Code, and Created columns are hidden on mobile viewports
test_cases.steps:
1. View the Holidays page on a mobile viewport.
2. Observe the table columns.
test_cases.expected: On mobile, the table shows only Name and Date columns. Location, Code, and Created columns are hidden to reduce clutter.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer is usable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. On a mobile device, tap the 'Add Holiday' button.
2. Fill in the Name, Date, and Location fields.
3. Submit the form.
test_cases.expected: The create drawer opens properly on mobile. All form fields are accessible, the virtual keyboard does not obscure inputs, and the form can be submitted successfully.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal is usable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. On a mobile device, tap the Delete action for a holiday.
2. Observe and interact with the confirmation modal.
test_cases.expected: The delete confirmation modal displays correctly on mobile. The Cancel and Confirm buttons are tappable and function as expected.

test_cases.scenario: Filters are accessible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. On a mobile device, navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Attempt to use the Search, Location, and Year filters.
test_cases.expected: All three filters are accessible and functional on mobile. The filter UI does not overflow the screen.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer opens and displays correctly on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. On a mobile device, tap a holiday row.
2. Observe the view drawer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer opens and fills the appropriate area of the mobile screen. All detail fields are readable and the footer buttons are tappable.

test_cases.scenario: Created holiday is associated with the correct location
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a holiday and select 'London' as the location.
2. After creation, open the holiday via the view drawer.
test_cases.expected: The Location field in the view drawer shows 'London', confirming the holiday is linked to the correct location.

test_cases.scenario: Location filter dropdown shows only locations configured in the system
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Open the Location filter dropdown.
test_cases.expected: The Location filter contains only the locations that are configured in the Locations module. It does not show deleted or inactive locations.

test_cases.scenario: Year filter reflects years that have holidays
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to the Holidays page.
2. Open the Year filter dropdown.
test_cases.expected: The Year filter shows years for which at least one holiday exists, making it easy to navigate by year.

test_cases.scenario: Holiday code is automatically generated on creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a new holiday.
2. Open the created holiday via the view drawer or table.
3. Observe the Code field.
test_cases.expected: A unique code is automatically generated for the holiday without requiring manual input from the user.

test_cases.scenario: Filtering by a location shows only holidays for that location
test_cases.steps:
1. Create two holidays — one for 'Dublin' and one for 'Berlin'.
2. On the Holidays page, filter by 'Dublin'.
test_cases.expected: Only the holiday associated with 'Dublin' is shown. The 'Berlin' holiday is not displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Holidays remain after editing without losing location association
test_cases.steps:
1. Edit an existing holiday's name.
2. Save the change.
3. Open the updated holiday in the view drawer.
test_cases.expected: The location association is preserved after editing. The Location field in the view drawer still shows the original location.

test_cases.scenario: Multiple holidays can exist for the same location
test_cases.steps:
1. Create two different holidays both assigned to the same location.
2. Filter the list by that location.
test_cases.expected: Both holidays appear in the filtered list. A location can have multiple holidays.
